title: Avoiding Variable Capture by Alpha-Renaming First
description: Rename the inner bound variable y to a fresh z before beta-reducing (λx.λy.x) y so the free argument y stays free.

steps.description: Line 1 starts with `(λx.λy.x) y`, where the outer argument `y` is a free variable and the inner lambda `λy.x` binds the same name `y`.

steps.question: Before substituting the free argument `y` for `x` inside `λy.x`, how do we rewrite `λy.x` so that `y` is not captured by `λy`?
steps.answer: We alpha-rename the inner bound parameter `y` to a fresh variable `z` (giving `(λx.λz.x) y`), because `z` is not free in the argument.

steps.description: Line 2 applies alpha equivalence (`=α`) to rename the bound parameter `y` to `z`, producing `(λx.λz.x) y` without changing the function's meaning.
Lines 3-4 now perform `[x := y] (λz.x)` safely: replacing `x` with `y` inside `λz.x` produces `λz.y`, a constant function that ignores its parameter `z` and returns the free `y`.
